chapter: Raymond Scott, Kirby and postwar bands
title: Charlie's Tavern and the Roseland building on 7th Avenue
summary: The band ran to Charlie's Tavern between radio sets, and Hinton and Leeman pin down where the building, Roseland and A&R studios stood.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: All I know is we worked together and he was a hard drinking man and a hard playing band, and this same period of time -- I don't know how many weeks it was -- just a few weeks -- we're on the air at 4:45 to 5:00 -- and we would run over to the old Charlie's Tavern, and we tipped the
elevator boy to wait for us, and we'd run over and he'd have the bar set up before we went on the air, because Raymond was a stickler for ...

That was 7th Avenue, right? And Charlie's Tavern was -- just to explain to the people that might not know, this is 7th Avenue between 50th Street and 51st Street, and 799 7th Avenue was on the right hand side going south, and Charlie's Tavern was on the left hand side.
In the Roseland building. The old Roseland building, and downstairs on the 51st Street side, I guess was the original Basin Street West. But we'll get to that afterwards. Now where were we?
We want the people to know a few years later, exactly where these places are.
You know, I think that office building is still there.

Well, no, the office building -- it's now the City Squire, which is turned into the Sheraton Hotel now, where that same place was. It's now the Sheraton there, Roseland and the Roosevelt was upstairs, and ...
